_comment: v3.66.1452. Re-run from a detached clone: toolchain/bin/bd-mutate --spec tests/mutants/v3_66_1452_shuffle_lane_containment.json --work DETACHED_CLONE. EVERY ANCHOR HERE IS STRUCTURAL ON PURPOSE -- no numeric literal, no quoted string, no True/False/None and no `=` -- because row357 refuses a new value-bearing anchor that no producer re-derives, and it was right to refuse the first draft of this battery: an anchor like `pytest-timeout>=2.0,<3.0` freezes a pin whose value a later cut may legitimately change, and the battery would then fail for a reason that has nothing to do with its subject. The replacement text carries the value; the anchor carries only shape. M6 is the one worth reading twice. It makes an EARLY refusal fail-open, and a LATER refusal inside the same tool still returns exit 4 -- so a catcher that asserted only the exit code would report CAUGHT while the defect shipped. It is caught because the assertion also requires that refusal's own distinctive remedy text (CLAUDE.md A5: when several refusals share an exit code, assert the distinctive diagnostic; A7's bd-vault-unlock note is the same lesson).
